signals.metric: off-CPU 'data page read' share of connection-thread time

signals.metric: swap in/out (pswpin/pswpout), PSI memory some/full, MemAvailable, major faults of mysqld
signals.condition: any sustained swap-in or memory PSI stall during the run
signals.why: an oversized pool plus per-session buffers pushes mysqld or the page cache into swap/OOM, which is far slower than a pool miss

impact_bound: Gain <= share of foreground time in data-page-read waits x fraction of those reads the extra memory would cache (estimate from the miss curve: compare Innodb_buffer_pool_reads at two sizes, or use pages read vs pool pages). Typical: high on I/O-bound workloads (2-10x), none when the working set fits.

experiment.change: raise the pool (online resize) in steps toward available RAM minus per-session and OS headroom
experiment.predict: Innodb_buffer_pool_reads/trx and data-page-read off-CPU share fall; disk read IOPS fall; throughput rises
experiment.confirm_or_refute: confirmed if reads/trx drop and throughput rises above noise; refuted if reads/trx do not drop (working set much larger or reads are scans/read-ahead) or swap/PSI appear
experiment.cost_or_risk: less memory for OS cache/sessions; swap or OOM if over-sized; longer warm-up

collected: yes (swap/PSI/memory, pool reads, wait_free, eBPF page-read waits, file I/O by type)
